title.en: Introduction and Basic Concepts of Thermodynamics

syllabus.topic: Scope and limitations of thermodynamics
System, surrounding, functions, properties and process
System — homogeneous and heterogeneous, closed and open, isolated system, state of system
Properties — extensive and intensive
Function — state and path function
Process — reversible and irreversible
Steady and equilibrium state
Thermal, chemical, mechanical and thermodynamic equilibrium
Force, pressure, work, power and energy
Gibb's phase rule, degree of freedom
Zeroth law of thermodynamics
Temperature
Ideal gas temperature scale
Simple examples (numerical) on force, pressure, work and energy, phase rule
First law of thermodynamics
Internal energy, enthalpy and heat capacity
First law for non-flow processes and flow process
Numerical based on first law and energy — internal energy, enthalpy and heat capacity
PVT behavior of pure fluids with PV and PT diagram
Ideal gas and equation of state
Ideal gas process — constant volume, constant pressure, constant temperature, adiabatic, polytropic
Equation of state for real gases — Van der Waals (brief), virial equation, compressibility charts
Numerical based on ideal gas and real gas equations
Limitations of the first law of thermodynamics
Heat reservoir, heat engine, heat pump
General statement of the second law
Concept of entropy
Carnot principle — thermodynamic temperature scale, ideal gas as Carnot engine working substance
Entropy change — phase change, ideal gas process, adiabatic mixing, isothermal mixing of ideal gases, chemical reaction
Clausius inequality
Mathematical statement of the second law
Numerical based on entropy change and heat engine efficiency
Statement of the third law of thermodynamics

course_outcomes: Understand the fundamental concepts of thermodynamics
Apply the concept of first law for flow and non-flow processes
Use equations of state for ideal and real gases to predict PVT behaviour
Apply the concept of second law of thermodynamics
Apply the laws of thermodynamics in refrigeration
